body:
Also, by doing it this way:
```js
const params = new URL(url, 'http://x').searchParams;
```
`url` can now be both absolute and relative.

**edit:**

In the ideal case, `next` would have the concept of a base url on the server, which can be used to make a `URL` polyfill that can handle relative urls serverside. It should also be not based on any request header as that is a security hazard. 
Same use case as described here https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/7262#issuecomment-490070989
It would also be very beneficial for the `fetch` polyfill of https://github.com/zeit/next.js/pull/7300
